prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; sends Transformer Tap Snapshot on transformer review request), Main Transformer, export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; dispatch boundary; authorized signals with transmission system). Public grid, port ops out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; blocks protection-conflicting commands; produces Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode if aux lost), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; blade imagery). Substation: Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Emergency Generator (Foxglove). Aux power: auto start on loss; transfer within V/f limits; no unapproved paralleling; not exported; shed nonessential; start-failure alarm; UPS control power; transfer back when stable. Grid Dispatcher sets dispatch; Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard) allocates output, uses Position Quality Flag, assigns vessel/crew to approved work packages after Duty Planner confirms; Control Engineer verifies settings; frequency response only in authorized mode; comms loss keeps local protection; export resumes only when stable; Substation Operator confirms switching; alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; work packages from Pitch Deviation Notice; Session Revocation Receipt), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; ranks work; uses Squall Window Bulletin; produces Deferred Task Rationale when weather prevents task, not implying safety), Operations Radio Console, Work Permit Portal. Duty Planner: ranks/mobilizes, checks parts, competence, conditions vs task/transfer/vessel limits; revises priorities on changes, communicates plan; safety faults first. Field Supervisor validates faults. Weather Service: forecasts+confidence; Metocean Buoy: local observations; Weather Analyst compares both, advises window reliability. Confidence not substitute for limits; low confidence near limit: conservative, shorter review. Weather Hold: outside limits or insufficient evidence; improved forecast alone doesn't release. Vessel Standby mode: transit/station keeping possible, transfer/task not justified. Marine Coordinator: daily plan, reassesses route/access, seeks updated forecast. Vessel Master receives Transfer Manifest Addendum before departure; approves/pauses/aborts approach. Quiet Harbor blocks route change if authorization incomplete. HSE Officer (Harness Audit Card); Storekeeper validates Backorder Exception Slip from Warehouse System (Mosslight). Port Agent; Rescue

New part:
S291: Work already in progress is reassessed if measured conditions approach a limit, and personnel are withdrawn when the safe margin is no longer adequate.
S292: The Duty Planner adjusts the executable plan when a delay, cancellation, or alternative access method changes resource demand.
S293: Decision records capture the forecast basis, applicable limits, observed conditions, and the reason for proceeding, holding, or returning to port.
S294: The Turbine Sensor Bus collects operating measurements from the Turbine Controller, Pitch System, Converter Cabinet, and Nacelle Condition Monitor.
S295: The SCADA Gateway forwards time-stamped observations to the Shore Control Room for review against configured operating limits.
S296: The monitoring process retains the source, timestamp, and turbine identifier for each observation so that abnormal readings can be traced to their origin.
S297: The Control Engineer reviews alarms alongside recent operating trends rather than treating an isolated threshold crossing as a confirmed fault.
S298: Validation checks cover sensor range, signal freshness, timestamp alignment, and consistency with related measurements.
S299: The Control Engineer compares disputed readings with independent signals from the Turbine Controller and Nacelle Condition Monitor where available.
S300: A stale or implausible value is marked as unverified and is not used alone to justify an intrusive maintenance task.
S301: Repeated or corroborated deviations are assessed for severity, persistence, and potential impact on safe turbine operation.
S302: The Control Engineer records the evidence considered and the basis for accepting, rejecting, or continuing to monitor an alert.
S303: The Shore Control Room escalates an alert when its severity exceeds the operating threshold or when the evidence indicates a developing hazard.
S304: The Duty Planner reviews accepted alerts for immediate response needs and for effects on the executable maintenance plan.
S305: Where a turbine response is required, the Control Engineer follows the approved operating procedure and confirms the resulting state through available indications.
S306: If an observation suggests a risk to personnel or equipment, the response prioritizes safe operation and restricts work until the condition is understood.
S307: The Offshore Substation is consulted when the event may affect electrical operation or require coordination beyond the turbine.
S308: The Maintenance Planning Engine receives validated condition information for prioritization and scheduling of follow-up work.
S309: The Weather Service and Metocean Buoy provide contextual conditions that help reviewers distinguish environmental effects from equipment deterioration.
S310: The Control Engineer requests an on-site inspection when remote evidence cannot resolve a material uncertainty.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
